blockers.title: The universal object-path and install-volume predicate cannot represent a mandatory pathless platform TCB class
evidence: OS ABI is a mandatory taxonomy class and its allowed evidence form is PLATFORM-ATTESTED. originSearchPolicy expressly permits classAppropriateLookup to be null when a class has no lookup.

The trace boundary nevertheless includes every system-class access attempt, while resolutionPredicate step 3 unconditionally requires an actual object path, symlink canonicalization, filesystem selection, and equality with the verifiedInstallRoot volume before the allowlist is consulted.

No pathless or non-file-backed event form exists, and no class- or entry-specific exception can replace install-root volume equality. An OS ABI attestation with no object path therefore cannot reach its exact allowlist match; by the contract's own failure rule the comparison is unmakeable and must refuse.

The same unconditional predicate rejects an otherwise exact declared system dependency whenever its signed canonical origin is on a different volume from the application install root. That defeats the purpose of a host-ABI/system-dependency allowlist rather than distinguishing declared from ambient origin.
blockers.impact: DR-G22 requires every complete profile times every taxonomy class unless the class is truly absent or inapplicable. OS ABI is not absent on a supported platform, yet v12 supplies no conforming evidence path through step 3, so the declared platform matrix cannot qualify under this contract.
blockers.requiredRepair: Make filesystem-volume evidence conditional on a closed file-backed form. Define a pathless PLATFORM-ATTESTED observation and join for classes such as OS ABI, and let signed originSearchPolicy state the lawful volume/origin constraint for external system objects. Preserve exact install-root volume equality only for entries whose signed policy actually requires it; define retained required/absent forms for each branch.

shouldFix.title: The repaired procfs rule selects the twenty-second token after comm instead of overall field 22
evidence: The rule says starttime is the twenty-second whitespace-separated field after the final ')' in /proc/<pid>/stat.

pid and the parenthesized comm are overall fields 1 and 2. The first token after the final ')' is therefore overall field 3 (state), so overall field 22 is the twentieth token after that delimiter, not the twenty-second.

Following the v12 instruction selects overall field 24 (rss), while both the identity shape and namespace binding treat that value as starttime. The final-parenthesis delimiter repair is sound; the post-delimiter offset is not.
shouldFix.impact: The before/after checks compare RSS rather than process start time. RSS can remain equal across PID reuse and can change without PID reuse, so the defense can both miss the replacement it is intended to detect and spuriously refuse a stable verifier. The namespace observation is then bound to the wrong process-identity value as well.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Locate the final ')' that terminates comm, treat the next token as overall field 3, and select the twentieth token after that delimiter (overall field 22, starttime; zero-based post-delimiter index 19). State both the overall field number and the post-delimiter index to remove the ambiguity.

shouldFix.title: preselectionRecord and laterEventVolumeFields are not closed or joined retained schemas
evidence: preselectionRecord declares kind=preselection, but retainedEventSchema's eventKind union contains only resolution-attempt, use, refusal, and inapplicable. The contract does not say that preselectionRecord is a separate run record, give it runIdentity, bind it to the event stream, or require exactly one such record per run. Meanwhile the old preselection-only labels remain in retainedEventSchema, creating a second possible placement.

evidenceJoin still names an undefined PreselectionFilesystemObservation instead of preselectionRecord. That token occurs nowhere else, and the join continues to compare a three-member observation to two later fields rather than naming the new volumeEquality rule or its record paths.

The claimed OS-tagged volume forms are only prose labels. No closed serialization exists for macOS f_fsid, Linux decodedMountPoint/device, or linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity; volumeEquality's statement that serialization is 'the closed form above' has no such form to reference.

laterEventVolumeFields makes observed volume and type unconditionally required, but a refusal caused by an unobservable or ambiguous volume cannot populate those values and has no tagged unavailable/refusal form. Extra fields are not rejected in either added object, so required/forbidden lists alone do not make them closed.
shouldFix.impact: A preselection baseline can be detached from or substituted across runs, producers can serialize unequal identities as if they matched, and mandatory fail-closed outcomes can be impossible to encode. The new names do not yet make the exact-volume decision independently checkable from retained evidence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define one exhaustive retained-run schema with runIdentity, subject/carrier bindings, and exactly one preselection record, or add preselection to a closed event-kind union with equivalent cardinality. Remove duplicate preselection fields from later events; define explicit tagged macOS and Linux identity objects and canonical serialization; define the Linux selected-record identity; join exact named paths; reject extras; and provide closed observed, unavailable, and inapplicable later-event variants.

advisories.title: verifiedInstallRoot equality conflates signed-token bytes with the host-local canonical path
advisories.evidence: normalization says NFC and UTF-8 occur before grammar validation and signing, while equality says UTF-8 byte equality is evaluated after NFC and after canonicalization. Canonicalization occurs only after the signed token is joined to host-local anchor A, so the signed token and runtime canonical target are different byte domains and can have different host prefixes and post-symlink spellings.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The normalization, join, and canonicalization operations are each otherwise named and fail closed, so the intended implementation can be inferred; the single equality sentence is the remaining ambiguity.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Split this into signedTokenEquality (UTF-8 bytes after NFC, before signing) and canonicalTargetEquality (the exact host-local canonical path identity after join), including whether canonical output is re-normalized or treated as filesystem-native bytes.

advisories.title: Before/after namespace-inode equality does not exclude an A-to-B-to-A namespace transition
advisories.evidence: Both clauses require equal ns/mnt inode observations before and after mountinfo, but neither holds a namespace handle across the read nor states that the verifier cannot change namespace. A transition from namespace A to B for the mountinfo open/read and back to A before the second observation passes the two equality checks while binding B's mount table to A's inode.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The observer is the qualification verifier rather than an untrusted payload, so a dedicated implementation can avoid namespace transitions; the contract should make that relied-upon invariant explicit.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Use a dedicated verifier whose mount namespace is immutable for the observation, or hold an open namespace handle and define an equivalent stable-read protocol that excludes ABA before retaining the baseline.
